subtype: Approach: collects suggestions from a wide community and looks for repeated patterns [Thinking]
passage:
'Sixty-two replies,' Jagdish said, scrolling. 'On the fresher post. Everyone wrote something different.'

Avni pulled the laptop closer. 'Bus timings. Library cards. Mess timings. The wifi password.'

'Wait,' said Jagdish. 'Read the ones I highlighted.'

'"Didn't know the gate closes at ten." "Nobody told me visitors aren't allowed." "Confused about laundry days."'

'All hostel rules,' said Jagdish. 'Fourteen of the sixty-two, more than any other topic. When the same thing turns up again and again from different people, it's not luck.'

'So orientation needs a hostel rules session?'

'Or one page. But first we check with the warden that these rules are the current ones.'

qa.q: How many of the replies mentioned hostel rules?
qa.a: Fourteen of the sixty-two replies mentioned hostel rules.

qa.q: What does Jagdish seem to feel about the repeated hostel replies?
qa.a: Jagdish feels sure and interested, having spotted a pattern that many freshers share.

qa.q: What could the club do with the hostel finding?
qa.a: The club could check the current rules with the warden, then add a short hostel session or a one-page sheet to orientation.

qa.q: How might a fresher who was confused about laundry days see the new session?
qa.a: That fresher would probably feel relieved that someone listened and cleared up the rules early.

grounding: Shows a club collecting online replies about orientation and noticing that many mention confusion about hostel rules.
